I would urgently flag the conflict to the duty manager: the box is on today’s destruction list despite a verified collection booking for Wednesday, and the contents are irreplaceable. I’d ask whether there is an authorised way to prevent destruction without changing the storage date.

I would **not change the date** on the strength of the pending request. Permission can only be registered at a sitting, and tomorrow’s decision might not be approval.

If no authorised protective solution were available by 13:30, I would leave the manifest unreleased rather than knowingly send this box for irreversible destruction. That would delay all 60 boxes and go against the manager’s instruction; I would report the incomplete shift and the reason openly, not present it as an approved extension.

I’d then follow up at Tuesday’s sitting. Only if written permission is registered would I enter the extension. If it is refused, the conflict still needs escalation; the booked collection cannot be assumed to have authorised extra storage.
